title: Evidence & proof drawer permanently empty: '0 events' and all evidence tabs blank after a fully completed verified session
user: first-time learner (also the exact surface a judge opens to check the verification claim)
environment: browser (Chrome), sample lesson leakage-01, no account
prerequisites: Complete the sample lesson end-to-end (transfer passed, patch verified) and land on /proof/<session>.
steps: Finish the sample lesson (Question -> Prediction -> Test -> Boundary -> Apply -> Repair).
On the proof page, observe the bottom bar 'Evidence & proof - 0 events'.
Click Open; visit tabs Activity, Plan, Diff, Tests, Verifier.
Reload /proof/<session> and repeat (still empty).
Compare with the downloaded proof record: 12 hash-chained events, publicTests passed, externalVerifier VERIFIED with named invariants.
expected: Drawer populates with the session's event chain, plan, diff, test results and verifier invariants; counter reflects the 12 recorded events.
actual: Counter reads '0 events' for the whole journey; after completion every tab shows 'No <activity/plan/diff/tests/verifier> evidence yet. It will appear here when the session produces it.' Only Provenance has content. State persists after full reload.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: All five tabs empty post-completion; persists after reload of /proof/session_db9778ae-2e82-456a-a193-9c03292e1eba

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: Downloaded proof bundle contains 12 events (session.created, belief_test.proposed/confirmed, prediction.committed, lab.compilation_started, lab.verified, experiment.completed, revision.recorded, transfer.started/passed, patch.compilation_started, patch.verified) and externalVerifier.status=VERIFIED

likely_cause: Drawer event feed is not wired to the session/proof event store (or is gated to live-notebook sessions only); empty-state copy assumes events exist ('when the session produces it').
unverified: Whether live (uploaded-notebook) sessions populate the drawer; live path could not be tested (no file upload).
learner_impact: At the reflective moment when a learner goes to check WHY they should trust the result, the product says no evidence exists - directly contradicting everything they just experienced.
judge_impact: High: the flagship verification surface appears broken in the primary demo path; undermines the core 'prove it' thesis on inspection.
trust_impact: Severe contradiction: UI claims 'verified' everywhere while the evidence drawer claims nothing was produced.
recommended_correction: Wire the drawer to the same event/artifact store that backs the proof download; show event chain, plan, diff, public-test report and verifier invariants per tab; fix the counter.
smallest_correction: For sample/replay sessions, render the recorded session's events and verifier invariants from the stored bundle instead of the live feed.
acceptance_criteria: After completing the sample, the drawer shows >=12 events with actor/kind, the Verifier tab lists the accepted invariants (e.g. baseline_overlap_exists, canonical_result_hash), Tests tab shows publicTests 1/0, Diff tab shows the cell-3 patch.
regression_test: Complete sample lesson in a fresh browser; open drawer; assert non-empty Activity and Verifier tabs and counter > 0.

title: Command palette 'Show verifier - Inspect accepted invariants and concrete rejections' routes to the empty Verifier tab
user: first-time learner / judge using CounterLab Studio palette
prerequisites: Completed sample session; open Commands (Ctrl K) palette.
steps: Open Project & evidence -> Commands Ctrl K.
Choose 'Show verifier'.
Verifier tab opens empty ('No verifier evidence yet').
expected: Accepted invariants and concrete rejections listed, as the command description promises.
actual: Same empty Verifier panel as A2-01; the palette over-promises.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Palette command opens Evidence & proof drawer on empty Verifier tab

likely_cause: Same root cause as A2-01 (drawer not fed); palette copy written against intended behavior.
learner_impact: A promised inspection surface delivers nothing; learner stops looking for proof.
judge_impact: Moderate: a judge following the obvious 'show verifier' path hits a dead end.
trust_impact: Promise/ delivery mismatch on the product's central claim.
recommended_correction: Fix drawer feed (A2-01); until then, point the command at the proof page's Technical proof section.
smallest_correction: Reword command to match current behavior or deep-link to the downloaded bundle contents.
acceptance_criteria: Show verifier displays the invariant list from the session bundle.
regression_test: After A2-01 fix, invoke palette command and assert invariant names visible.

title: Provenance tab shows stale/contradictory states after verification ('Boundary: Locked until verification', 'Capsule: Issued after verified repair')
prerequisites: Completed sample with verified patch; open drawer > Provenance.
steps: Complete lesson.
Open Evidence & proof > Provenance.
Read Boundary and Capsule rows.
expected: Post-verification states: boundary verified/released; capsule issued (with id/hash).
actual: 'Boundary: Locked until verification' and 'Capsule: Issued after verified repair' are shown even though lab.verified and patch.verified events already exist; reads as stale or as unexplained rule text rather than status.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Provenance rows contradict session state post-completion (Boundary 'Locked until verification'; Capsule 'Issued after verified repair')

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: Bundle events 6 (lab.verified) and 12 (patch.verified) precede the observation

likely_cause: Static placeholder strings in the Provenance panel, not bound to session state.
unverified: Whether the states ever flip (could not find any UI where they do).
learner_impact: Learner cannot tell whether their proof was actually sealed/issued.
judge_impact: Moderate: provenance panel looks unfinished on inspection.
recommended_correction: Bind Boundary/Capsule rows to session state and show capsule id + hash once issued.
smallest_correction: Change copy to explicit status values derived from the bundle ('Boundary: verified', 'Capsule: issued - proof_<id>').
acceptance_criteria: Post-completion, Provenance shows verified boundary and issued capsule identifier matching the downloaded bundle.
regression_test: Complete sample; assert Provenance rows match bundle state.

title: Codex is invisible across the entire learner-facing UI; it appears only inside the downloaded proof JSON and as replay metadata 'Model: gpt-5.6-sol'
user: first-time learner; OpenAI Build Week judge
devpost_criterion: OpenAI Build Week - demonstrable Codex usage
steps: Scan homepage and every wizard screen for any mention of Codex/OpenAI/model identity.
Complete the lesson and inspect the repair diff screen (the Codex-produced artifact) - no authorship shown.
Download the proof record: events 5 and 11 carry actor='codex' (lab.compilation_started, patch.compilation_started); generatedAdapter carries sha256+commitHash.
Open /replay/leakage-01: metadata shows 'Model: gpt-5.6-sol' - the only UI surface naming a model.
expected: Codex-authored artifacts (adapter, patch) are attributed in-UI where they appear, consistent with the proof chain's actor model.
actual: No Codex/model attribution anywhere in the product UI; attribution exists only in the downloaded machine-readable bundle and one replay metadata row.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Zero Codex mentions on homepage, all 6 wizard steps, proof page, drawers, palette

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: proof bundle events with actor='codex'; generatedAdapter sha256 ed70072a..., commit 1050fa76...

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Replay metadata 'Model: gpt-5.6-sol'

likely_cause: Attribution surfaced only in the proof bundle schema, never projected into UI components.
unverified: Whether Judge Mode (/judge) surfaces Codex usage (assigned to another agent).
learner_impact: Low for learning; relevant to 'what is generated?' comprehension (cold-pass Q9 unanswerable).
judge_impact: High for an OpenAI Build Week submission: a judge using the product cannot see where Codex is used without downloading and reading JSON.
trust_impact: Generated artifacts (reframed explanation, patch diff) look hand-authored; provenance story incomplete.
recommended_correction: Attribute Codex-generated artifacts in place: e.g. 'Patch generated by Codex (model gpt-5.6-sol, commit 4f2f6472), verified by leakage-verifier-v1' on the diff; mark the explanation reframe as AI-generated (see A2-15).
smallest_correction: Add one provenance line under the verified notebook change and under 'Your current explanation' naming the generator model.
acceptance_criteria: A learner can state where Codex appears after using the product; attribution matches bundle actor/model fields.
regression_test: Text search for 'Codex' or model id on /session and /proof pages in E2E test.

title: Homepage fails first-20-seconds comprehension: audience, prediction mechanic, verified-vs-generated distinction and Codex are all absent; trust sentence is jargon-dense
user: first-time learner with no notebook and no prior context
devpost_criterion: Education track - accessibility of learning experience; demo clarity
steps: Load / and read only above-the-fold content for ~20 seconds.
Attempt to answer: what is this, who is it for, what problem, what to do, why prediction, difference from AI explanation, where is Codex, what is verified, what is generated, live/sample/replay.
expected: A first-timer can answer most of the 10 questions from the fold.
actual: Questions 2 (who), 5 (why prediction), 7 (Codex), 8 (what is verified), 9 (what is generated) unanswerable; 1, 3, 4, 6, 10 only partially. 'CI for understanding', 'fixed kernels', 'frozen checks', 'evidence binding' unexplained. Four CTAs compete with no newcomer routing. The clearest thesis line ('Chatbots explain. CounterLab lets reality answer.') and the word 'Education' appear only inside a session footer.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Cold-pass transcript and 10-question table in 03_FIRST_TIME_LEARNER_AUDIT.md section 1

likely_cause: Fold optimized for atmosphere over comprehension; key explainer copy lives in-session; no 'how it works' visual.
unverified: Intended audience may be judges rather than true learners; /judge may carry the framing.
learner_impact: Learner starts without a mental model of the loop they are about to enter; prediction-first mechanic is a surprise.
judge_impact: Moderate: judges get the thesis quickly via sample, but the product's education identity is not self-evident from the landing page.
trust_impact: Trust words without referents read as marketing.
recommended_correction: Add one concrete above-the-fold line naming audience + loop ('A learning lab for ML evidence: predict, watch a fair test falsify or confirm, repair.'), move the 'Chatbots explain...' line up, and gloss the trust sentence in plain words.
smallest_correction: Replace the tagline block with: 'For learners with a Python notebook: state what you believe your result means, lock a prediction, and watch a verified fair test answer - not a chatbot.'
acceptance_criteria: Cold users can answer 8/10 questions in hallway testing; 'prediction' appears on the fold.
regression_test: Snapshot test asserting key explainer strings present on /.

title: 'How proof works' rail link produces no visible response
user: first-time learner seeking the promised explanation of proof
steps: On /, click 'How proof works' in the left rail.
expected: A modal, page, or anchored section explaining proof (kernels, checks, refusal).
actual: No navigation, modal, scroll, or expansion; only the link's active styling changes. The one-line 'How proof works:' summary on the fold remains the only explanation.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Click produced no visible change across repeated attempts

likely_cause: Anchor target missing or link bound to a section that does not exist on the single-viewport page.
unverified: Whether it is meant to deep-link into a docs page that is unbuilt.
learner_impact: The one place that promises to decode the jargon does nothing; trust words stay unexplained.
judge_impact: Low-moderate: looks like a dead control in the primary nav.
trust_impact: Minor; broken affordance on the core claim.
recommended_correction: Open a short proof explainer (what is fixed, what is generated, what is verified, what is refused) with a concrete example.
smallest_correction: Remove the link or point it at the replay page, which already demonstrates the concept.
regression_test: E2E click test asserting visible explainer container.

title: Verdict language 'This is the deceptive random-split headline under test' is shown BEFORE the learner locks a prediction
prerequisites: Enter a claim and reach step 2.
steps: Read the evidence chip 'Cell 3 - output 0' on the Prediction screen before sealing an expectation.
expected: Neutral evidence presentation until the prediction is locked; evaluative language after the result.
actual: The chip calls the 0.985 headline 'deceptive' pre-commit, signaling the 'right' answer; similarly the collapsed 'Why?' text on step 1 telegraphs the generalization catch. The falsification loses force for attentive readers.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Chip text verbatim: 'This is the deceptive random-split headline under test. accuracy: 0.985'

likely_cause: Cell-output caption written from the post-hoc narrator voice; not gated behind the lock.
unverified: Whether wording differs in live sessions.
learner_impact: Reduces genuine commitment/surprise; a cue-seeking learner guesses 'Fall materially' without understanding.
judge_impact: Moderate: undermines the signature 'locked prediction' mechanic on close reading.
trust_impact: Minor: the app appears to have prejudged the 'verified' outcome.
recommended_correction: Pre-lock, caption outputs neutrally ('The notebook's reported headline. accuracy: 0.985'); reveal evaluative framing after the result.
smallest_correction: Delete the word 'deceptive' from the pre-lock caption.
acceptance_criteria: No outcome-judging adjectives appear before prediction.committed in the event chain's UI.
regression_test: DOM assertion at step 2: absence of 'deceptive' before seal.

title: Prediction step does the thinking for the learner: app authors both explanations and both predictions; learner only clicks 'Yes, this captures my view'; confidence preset to 72%
steps: Observe that 'Your current explanation' and 'Alternative CounterLab will test' arrive pre-written with 'Predicts' statements.
Confirm view; observe seal UI options each carry app-written rationales and a 72% confidence preset.
Note that no free-text or numeric prediction is required.
expected: Learner generates at least one part of the prediction themselves (own words or number) before seeing app-framed alternatives.
actual: The only required learner inputs are a claim sentence, one radio choice, and optional confidence. Click-through without thinking is possible at the product's signature step.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Confirmation-only flow; seal UI disabled until radio chosen; slider preset 72%

likely_cause: Scaffolding chosen for reliability over generative learning; radio options bound to fixed lesson models.
unverified: Whether live sessions require more learner-authored prediction.
learner_impact: Weak generation effect; commitment is real (lock + confidence) but shallow.
judge_impact: Moderate: judges probing the 'locked prediction' claim find it is a confirm-click.
recommended_correction: Ask for a free-text or numeric expectation first, then show the categorical options as calibration; carry the learner's own words into the sealed card and Reasoning Diff.
smallest_correction: Remove the 72% preset (start empty) and require a one-line 'why I expect this' before sealing.
acceptance_criteria: Sealed prediction contains at least one learner-authored token beyond a radio id.
regression_test: E2E: seal button remains disabled until learner-authored input present.

title: Sample mode mislabels provenance: 'Uploaded notebook evidence' and 'The original upload will not be overwritten' although the learner uploaded nothing
steps: Read the evidence card title on step 1.
Read the repair preview on step 6.
expected: Sample-mode copy: 'Sample notebook evidence', 'the original sample notebook'.
actual: Copy says 'Uploaded notebook evidence' and 'The original upload will not be overwritten'. Header badge 'INSTANT SAMPLE' mitigates but the component-level labels conflict.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Card title and repair-preview copy verbatim

likely_cause: Shared components reuse live-session copy without a sample-mode variant.
learner_impact: Small confusion about whose notebook this is; blurs the sample/live distinction the product otherwise labels well.
trust_impact: Minor provenance inaccuracy in a product whose differentiator is provenance accuracy.
recommended_correction: Parametrize provenance copy by session mode (sample/live/replay).
smallest_correction: Replace 'Uploaded' with 'Sample notebook evidence (instant demo)' when mode=sample.
acceptance_criteria: No upload language in sample mode.
regression_test: Snapshot assertion on evidence card title in sample session.

title: 'Run the fair test' implies live computation, but the sample result is a recorded fixture replayed in the Worker
steps: Reach the 'Run the fair test' CTA.
Click; result appears instantly.
Inspect proof bundle: versions.environment='Cloudflare Worker with recorded local Docker runner evidence'; verifiedResultSet fixture descriptor (480 customers, 2880 rows, sha256).
expected: CTA wording matches reality: e.g. 'Reveal the verified result' for recorded sessions; 'Run' reserved for live compute.
actual: Button says 'Run'; the fair-test card honestly says 'result not released' two lines above, and badges say 'Verified sample' / 'Result authority: Fixed kernel' - partial mitigation - but the verb promises execution that does not occur in this environment.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: CTA 'Run the fair test'; instant result reveal

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: recorded local Docker runner evidence + fixture descriptor in proof bundle

likely_cause: Single CTA component shared across live and recorded modes.
unverified: Whether live sessions actually execute in the Worker (upload untestable).
learner_impact: Attentive learners may form a wrong model of where verification happens.
judge_impact: Moderate: judges probing 'is it live?' find the wording overstates liveness in the demo path.
trust_impact: Wording/provenance mismatch on the central action.
recommended_correction: Mode-aware CTA: sample/replay -> 'Reveal the verified result'; live -> 'Run the fair test'.
smallest_correction: Rename sample-mode CTA to 'See the verified result'.
acceptance_criteria: CTA verb matches session mode and bundle environment description.
regression_test: Snapshot assertion of CTA text per mode.

title: Heavy unexplained jargon across the journey with no glossary (entity leakage, identity ablation, entity boundary, fixed kernel, frozen checks, Subject Pack, Reasoning Diff, Proof Capsule, ROC AUC, the tutor, ...)
user: first-time learner without ML evaluation background
devpost_criterion: Education track - accessibility to target learners
steps: Read each screen as a non-ML learner; collect undefined terms (see jargon inventory in 03_FIRST_TIME_LEARNER_AUDIT.md section 3).
expected: Core concepts (entity leakage, boundary, verification) get one-line definitions at first use or on hover; specialist metadata (Subject Pack, release state) stays in technical panels.
actual: 30+ undefined terms; the flagship concept 'entity leakage' is never defined in plain language during the lesson that teaches it; 'the tutor' appears exactly once with no antecedent; history status 'REASONING DIFF ISSUED' is jargon.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Jargon inventory of 30+ terms across all screens

likely_cause: Terminology imported from the proof/verification domain without a learner-facing layer.
unverified: Target audience may be ML-adjacent learners for whom part of the register is fine.
learner_impact: Cognitive load competes with the actual lesson; learners may nod along without being able to name what they learned.
judge_impact: Moderate: depth reads as sophistication, but education judges may probe definitional support.
recommended_correction: First-use inline definitions + a glossary; plain-language aliases ('fair test', 'who is in the test set') alongside technical terms.
smallest_correction: Add a one-sentence plain definition of entity leakage at step 1 and of 'verified' at first badge.
acceptance_criteria: Core five terms defined at first use.

title: Experiment Theater 'Explore' tab is a dead-end in sample mode: advertises interactive knobs ('change split boundary, identity feature, entity field, test size') with no controls and no onward CTA
steps: Click Explore tab in sample mode.
expected: Either disabled-with-explanation, or one safe sample knob (e.g. test size) that actually recomputes, or an explicit 'upload a notebook to unlock' CTA.
actual: Copy invites interaction; only a notice card appears ('SAMPLE RESULT STAYS FIXED FOR A REPRODUCIBLE LESSON'). Honest labeling, but the tab promises what it cannot deliver and offers no next action.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Explore tab contains a single notice card

likely_cause: Live-only controls hidden in sample mode without a sample-specific design.
learner_impact: Minor letdown at the curiosity peak; a visible 'why not' is present but no path forward.
recommended_correction: Add one deterministic sample knob with kernel recompute, or a prominent 'Try with your own notebook' CTA.
smallest_correction: Rename tab 'Explore (live notebooks)' and add the upload CTA inline.
acceptance_criteria: Learner is never invited to interact with absent controls without a path.
regression_test: Assertion that sample-mode Explore contains either a control or a CTA.

title: Wizard header never marks step 6 (Repair) complete - checkmarks stop at Apply even on the proof page after a verified patch
prerequisites: Complete lesson; view proof page; reload.
steps: Observe wizard header steps 1-5 ticked, 6 Repair unticked on /proof.
Reload; same.
expected: Repair ticked once patch.verified exists (or header replaced by a completion state).
actual: Step 6 perpetually pending, contradicting the page's own 'verified notebook change' content.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Header state unchanged after completion and reload

likely_cause: Completion flag for step 6 not set on transition to /proof, or header not re-rendered.
learner_impact: Small 'am I done?' ambiguity at the finale.
recommended_correction: Mark Repair complete when patch verification is issued.

title: No way to resume or revisit a completed session from the homepage; history exists only inside an active session's Studio drawer
prerequisites: Complete the sample once; return to /.
steps: Complete lesson.
Navigate to /.
Look for recent session / continue / my proofs.
expected: A 'Recent sessions' / 'Continue' affordance on the landing page.
actual: Homepage is byte-identical to the cold state; the completed session ('REASONING DIFF ISSUED') is reachable only by opening a (new) session and using Project & evidence > Recent sessions, or by bookmarking the /proof URL.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Cold-identical homepage after completion; history entry present in Studio drawer

likely_cause: Session history (localStorage) surfaced only in the in-app drawer, not on the landing page.
unverified: Whether 'Start with evidence' rail label is intended to become a history link.
learner_impact: Revisiting one's proof (step 12 of the thesis) requires insider knowledge; spaced review is effectively unsupported.
judge_impact: Moderate: the advertised 'replayable proof' loop is hard to re-enter.
recommended_correction: Render recent sessions with proof links on / when history exists.
smallest_correction: Add a 'Resume last session' link on the homepage when an active session exists.
acceptance_criteria: A returning learner reaches their proof in one click from /.
regression_test: E2E: complete sample, visit /, assert recent-session link.

title: AI-reframed 'Your current explanation' is presented under the learner's name with no generated-by label
steps: Compare typed claim ('...almost always right') with the displayed 'Your current explanation' ('The notebook's random-row test accuracy demonstrates generalization to new customers.').
expected: Reframed text visibly marked as AI-generated interpretation (matching the product's own distinction between learner input and generated content).
actual: The reframing is shown as 'Your current explanation' with an Edit button; nothing marks it as machine-generated, while the product elsewhere stresses fixed-vs-generated distinctions.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Reframed explanation text differs materially from typed claim; no provenance tag

likely_cause: Empathetic labeling ('Your') chosen for ownership; provenance tag omitted.
unverified: Whether the reframe is model-generated per session or template-based (bundle shows a codex actor for lab compilation; the reframe's origin is unverified).
learner_impact: Learner may not notice their idea was reworded (here: strengthened into testable form); blurs the learner-input vs AI-interpretation boundary the audit is asked to check.
trust_impact: Misattribution of generated content to the learner.
recommended_correction: Label: 'CounterLab's restatement of your claim (AI-generated) - edit until it says what you mean.'
smallest_correction: Add a small 'AI restatement - editable' tag on the card.
acceptance_criteria: Generated interpretation visually distinct from verbatim learner input.
regression_test: Presence assertion of the provenance tag at step 2.

title: Replay step copy says 'CounterLab has now run and checked the fairer test', conflicting with the replay page's own 'not a live model run' banner
prerequisites: Open /replay/leakage-01 and continue the replay to the Test step.
steps: Read the recorded-replay banner, then the Test-step copy after 'Continue replay'.
expected: Replay-aware copy ('CounterLab ran and checked the fairer test; this is the recorded result').
actual: Present-perfect 'has now run' sits under a banner stating nothing is running.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Banner + step copy on same screen

likely_cause: Step copy shared between live and replay modes.
learner_impact: Minor tense confusion; replay labeling is otherwise exemplary.
trust_impact: Minor inconsistency on an otherwise strong surface.
smallest_correction: Change to past tense in replay mode.
acceptance_criteria: No present-tense execution claims in replay mode.
regression_test: Snapshot assertion on replay step copy.

title: Proof-page finale is emotionally flat and offers no onward learning path (no consolidation moment, no next-lesson or own-notebook CTA)
user: first-time learner at the payoff moment
steps: Read the proof page top-to-bottom as a learner.
expected: A brief consolidation of what changed in the learner's understanding (e.g. restating the falsified belief vs the verified rule) plus a next action: try your own notebook / next concept (class imbalance) / replay.
actual: One summary line ('You can now distinguish...'), the Reasoning Diff table, technical material and downloads; the only onward actions are file downloads. The second supported concept (class imbalance) is never offered as a next step.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Proof page composition

likely_cause: Proof page optimized for audit artifacts over learning closure.
unverified: Whether a class-imbalance lesson exists elsewhere (none offered on this path).
learner_impact: The learning arc ends on documentation, not reflection; transfer momentum is lost.
recommended_correction: Add a consolidation block ('You believed X; the fair test showed Y; your rule is now Z') and CTAs: 'Try your own notebook', 'Next: class imbalance', 'Watch replay'.

acceptance_criteria: At least one onward learning action present on /proof.
